(card-moe_pqe)=
## Moe & Di Stefano (2017) P–q–e statistics

✅ verified · 3 equations · 1 source · [API: `MoeDiStefano2017Full`](../30-api/imf.md#api-imf-moedistefano2017full)

The faithful non-separable multiplicity statistics: mass-ratio power laws with a twin excess, all conditioned on primary mass AND period (Table 13 grids), plus the period- and mass-dependent eccentricity slope. The companion-composition engine behind MoeCompanions / MoeDiStefano2017Full.

| Use it for | Not for |
|---|---|
| ✓ observationally faithful binary populations across 0.8-40+ Msun primaries | ✗ separable q-only toys (use FlatMassRatio / PowerLawMassRatio) |
| ✓ massive-star population synthesis where the q-P coupling matters (twin excess at short P) | ✗ sub-solar primaries below the MD17 calibration range |

### Parameters

| Name | Meaning | Units | Typical range | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `primary_mass` | primary mass M1 conditioning every grid lookup | Msun | 0.8–40 (Table 13 bins, interpolated) | `MoeCompanions()/MoeDiStefano2017Full() consume M1 arrays at sample time` |

### Equations

```{math}
:label: card-gq-form
\begin{aligned} g(q\mid M_1,P)&=\frac{\phi(q)+A_t\,\mathbf{1}_{[0.95,1]}(q)/0.05}{I_A+I_B+A_t},\\ A_t&=\frac{F I_B}{1-F},\qquad q\in[q_{\min},1]. \end{aligned}
```

*Symbols:* $q$: mass ratio m2/m1; density zero outside [q_min, 1] [dimensionless]; $\phi(q)$: q^gamma_smallq below q_b, q_b^(gamma_smallq-gamma_largeq) q^gamma_largeq above; continuous at q_b [dimensionless]; $q_b$: power-law break, 0.3 in the retained default [dimensionless]; $I_A$: integral of phi from q_min to q_b [dimensionless]; $I_B$: integral of phi from q_b to 1 [dimensionless]; $F$: excess twin fraction within q > q_b; A_t/(I_B+A_t)=F, distinct from total q > 0.95 fraction [dimensionless]; $A_t$: unnormalized mass of uniform excess block [0.95, 1] [dimensionless]; $M_1$: primary mass conditioning the grid [Msun]; $P$: orbital period conditioning the grid [day].
*Assumes:* retained default q_min=0.1, q_b=0.3; uniform excess block on [0.95, 1]; Table-13 grid interpolation in (M1, log P); implementation clamps outside grid nodes, without wider-domain empirical qualification; local normalization of existing implementation; period-averaged Gaussian mixture is a separate model.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/mass-ratio-distributions.md#gq-full).

```{math}
:label: card-moe-eta-ecc
\eta(M_1, P) = \begin{cases} 0.6 - \dfrac{0.7}{\log_{10} P - 0.5}, & 0.8 < M_1 < 3\,M_\odot\ \text{(Eq. 17)} \\ 0.9 - \dfrac{0.2}{\log_{10} P - 0.5}, & M_1 > 7\,M_\odot\ \text{(Eq. 18)} \end{cases}
```

*Symbols:* $\eta$: eccentricity power-law slope p(e) proportional to e^eta (0 = uniform, 1 = thermal) [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* linear interpolation in M1 across 3-7 Msun; eta <= -1 (very short P) returns e ~ 0.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/binaries/eccentricity.md#moe-eta-ecc).

```{math}
:label: card-moe-emax-ecc
e_{\max}(P) \;=\; 1 - \Bigl(\frac{P}{2\,\mathrm{d}}\Bigr)^{-2/3} \quad (P > 2\ \mathrm{d})
```

*Symbols:* $e_{\max}$: period-dependent Roche-lobe eccentricity ceiling; P <= 2 d circularizes [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* components must not overflow Roche lobes at periapsis (MD17 Eq. 3).
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/binaries/eccentricity.md#moe-emax-ecc).

### Sources

- {cite:t}`MoeDiStefano2017` — Table 13 multiplicity grids (gamma_largeq, gamma_smallq, F_twin, f_logP) — ledger-verified cell-by-cell; eccentricity slopes and the Roche ceiling *(Table 13, p. 52; Eqs. 17-18 (eta fits); Eq. 3, p. 38 (e_max Roche ceiling))*

- code: [`MoeCompanions`](https://github.com/jaxstro/progenax/blob/main/src/progenax/binaries/companions.py) (`src/progenax/binaries/companions.py`)

(card-period_distributions)=
## Period distributions (Öpik / DM91 / Sana+2012)

✅ verified · 2 equations · 2 sources · [API: `LogUniformPeriod`](../30-api/binaries.md#api-binaries-loguniformperiod)

The three direct period samplers: log-uniform (Öpik baseline), the Duquennoy & Mayor (1991) solar-type log-normal, and the Sana+2012 short-period-biased OB power law — plus mass-dependent routing between them.

| Use it for | Not for |
|---|---|
| ✓ solar-type primaries: LogNormalPeriod (DM91 sec 7.3 defaults) | ✗ compact binaries / post-interaction periods (IC-time statistics only) |
| ✓ O/B primaries: SanaOBPeriod (pi = -0.55 in log10 P) | ✗ a generic low-mass field population sampled with the Sana OB law |
| ✓ mixed populations via MassDependentBinaryConfig routing at m_break |  |

### Parameters

| Name | Meaning | Units | Typical range | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mu_log_P` | log-normal mean of log10(P/day) (DM91: 4.8, median ~180 yr) | dex(day) | 4.8 | `LogNormalPeriod(mu_log_P=...)` |
| `sigma_log_P` | log-normal width (DM91: 2.3) | dex | 2.3 | `LogNormalPeriod(sigma_log_P=...)` |
| `power` | Sana OB slope pi of f(log10 P) proportional to (log10 P)^pi | dimensionless | -0.55 (+/- 0.2, Sana 2012) | `SanaOBPeriod(power=-0.55)` |

### Equations

```{math}
:label: card-dm91-lognormal
f(\log P) \;=\; C\,\exp\!\left[-\frac{(\log P - \overline{\log P})^2}{2\,\sigma_{\log P}^2}\right], \qquad \overline{\log P} = 4.8,\ \sigma_{\log P} = 2.3
```

*Symbols:* $P$: orbital period in days [day].
*Assumes:* solar-type primaries (DM91 sample).

```{math}
:label: card-sana-period
f(\log_{10} P) \;\propto\; (\log_{10} P)^{\pi}, \qquad \pi = -0.55,\ \ 0.15 \le \log_{10} P \le 3.5
```

*Symbols:* $\pi$: Sana 2012 period exponent (short-period biased) [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* O/B primaries; intrinsic (bias-corrected) distribution.

### Sources

- {cite:t}`DuquennoyMayor1991` — the solar-type Gaussian in log P (mean 4.8, sigma 2.3, P in days) *(Section 7.3 (per-paper note, PDF-verified; scanned source))*
- {cite:t}`Sana2012` — the OB-star intrinsic period power law pi = -0.55 +/- 0.2 *(Table S3 exponents (per-paper note))*

### Code & validation

- code: [`LogUniformPeriod`](https://github.com/jaxstro/progenax/blob/main/src/progenax/binaries/period.py) (`src/progenax/binaries/period.py`)
- code: [`LogNormalPeriod`](https://github.com/jaxstro/progenax/blob/main/src/progenax/binaries/period.py) (`src/progenax/binaries/period.py`)

(card-eccentricity)=
## Eccentricity distributions (thermal / uniform / Moe)

✅ verified · 2 equations · 2 sources · [API: `ThermalEccentricity`](../30-api/binaries.md#api-binaries-thermaleccentricity)

The three eccentricity samplers: Heggie's thermal f(e) = 2e (dynamical equilibrium), the uniform baseline, and the Moe & Di Stefano period-and-mass-dependent power law with the Roche ceiling.

| Use it for | Not for |
|---|---|
| ✓ dynamically processed populations: ThermalEccentricity (f = 2e, <e> = 2/3) | ✗ post-tidal-circularization populations at short P without the Moe ceiling |
| ✓ observationally faithful primordial e: MoeEccentricity (couples to P, M1) |  |

### Parameters

| Name | Meaning | Units | Typical range | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `e_max` | optional hard ceiling on ThermalEccentricity/UniformEccentricity draws | dimensionless | 0.9–1.0 | `ThermalEccentricity(e_max=...)` |

### Equations

```{math}
:label: card-thermal
f(e) \;=\; 2e,\qquad e \in [0, 1]
```

*Symbols:* $e$: orbital eccentricity [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* ideal full-support law e_max=1; mean 2/3 and draw sqrt(u); released ThermalEccentricity defaults e_max=0.99: draw e_max*sqrt(u), density 2e/e_max^2, mean 2e_max/3.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/binaries/eccentricity.md#thermal).

```{math}
:label: card-uniform-ecc
f(e) \;=\; 1,\qquad e \in [0, 1]
```

*Symbols:* $e$: orbital eccentricity [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* ideal interval [0,1] has mean 1/2; released UniformEccentricity defaults [0,0.9]; on [e_min,e_max], density 1/(e_max-e_min), mean (e_min+e_max)/2.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/binaries/eccentricity.md#uniform-ecc).

### Sources

- {cite:t}`Heggie1975` — the thermal/equilibrium f(e) = 2e from energy equipartition (with <e> = 2/3; CDF e^2, PPF sqrt(u)) *(per-paper note (heggie-1975.md), thermal-distribution discussion)*
- {cite:t}`MoeDiStefano2017` — the period/mass-dependent eta slope and the Roche e_max ceiling (see the moe_pqe card) *(Eqs. 17-18; Eq. 3, p. 38)*

### Code & validation

- code: [`UniformEccentricity`](https://github.com/jaxstro/progenax/blob/main/src/progenax/binaries/eccentricity.py) (`src/progenax/binaries/eccentricity.py`)

(card-kepler_elements)=
## Kepler orbital elements

✅ verified · 3 equations · 1 source · [API: `KeplerElements`](../30-api/binaries.md#api-binaries-keplerelements)

The two-body orbital-element chain: Kepler III (P <-> a), the Kepler equation solved by fixed-iteration Newton, true anomaly, orbit-plane state, and the 3-1-3 Euler rotation to inertial components — the machinery that turns (P, e, angles) into positions and velocities.

| Use it for | Not for |
|---|---|
| ✓ resolving sampled binaries into component positions/velocities (the binary -> spatial connector) | ✗ N >= 3 hierarchical dynamics (no secular evolution here) |
| ✓ machine-precision two-body ICs (energy/L conserved to ~1e-16) | ✗ relativistic or tidally evolving orbits |

### Parameters

| Name | Meaning | Units | Typical range | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `elements` | KeplerElements(a, e, i, omega, Omega, M0): semi-major axis, eccentricity, inclination, argument of periapsis, longitude of ascending node, mean anomaly | pc / dimensionless / rad | e in [0, 1); angles in [0, 2 pi) | `KeplerElements(a=..., e=..., i=..., omega=..., Omega=..., M0=...)` |

### Equations

```{math}
:label: card-kepler-third
P^2 \;=\; \frac{4\pi^2\,a^3}{G\,(m_1 + m_2)}
```

*Symbols:* $P$: orbital period [Myr (or day via unit conversion)]; $a$: semi-major axis of the RELATIVE orbit [pc].
*Assumes:* two-body; G explicit and units-carried.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/binaries/kepler-elements.md#kepler-third).

```{math}
:label: card-kepler-eq
E - e\,\sin E \;=\; M(t), \qquad M(t) = M_0 + n\,t,\quad n = 2\pi/P
```

*Symbols:* $E$: eccentric anomaly (fixed-iteration Newton solve — differentiable, JIT-safe) [rad]; $M$: mean anomaly [rad].
*Assumes:* fixed iteration count (no while_loop): converged to float64 for e < 0.99.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/binaries/kepler-elements.md#kepler-eq).

```{math}
:label: card-components
\mathbf{r}_1 = -\frac{m_2}{m_1 + m_2}\,\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{rel}}, \qquad \mathbf{r}_2 = +\frac{m_1}{m_1 + m_2}\,\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{rel}}
```

*Symbols:* $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{rel}}$: relative separation vector after the 3-1-3 Euler rotation [pc].
*Assumes:* center-of-mass frame: momentum exactly zero per binary.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/binaries/kepler-elements.md#components).

### Sources

- {cite:t}`MurrayDermott2000` — the standard celestial-mechanics chain (Kepler equation, anomalies, orbit-plane state, Euler rotations) *(Ch. 2 (the two-body problem))*

(card-binary_cluster_assembly)=
## Binary-cluster assembly (legacy and cataloged APIs)

✅ verified · 1 equation · 2 sources · [API: `build_binary_cluster`](../30-api/builders.md#api-builders-build_binary_cluster)

The composition operator: primary IMF x companion model x population target -> a cluster whose binaries are resolved into components (resolve_binary_components) with per-binary COM preservation and full primordial-pair bookkeeping. build_cataloged_binary_cluster retains stable birth IDs, sampled elements, and periapsis contact margins; the legacy build_binary_cluster return contract remains unchanged. Both wrappers share one physical construction. A semantics card — the physics lives in the composed model cards. IMF/companion masses and TotalMass budgets use solar masses; the shared construction converts masses to native dynamical units. Stellar radii remain in R_sun; orbital axes and contact margins use the position length unit. Deterministic unit checks do not qualify wider domains.

| Use it for | Not for |
|---|---|
| ✓ one-call binary-population ICs (Systems / Stars / TotalMass targets) | ✗ hierarchical triples+ (pairs only at IC time) |
| ✓ energy-budget-aware binary populations (binary_energy_budget diagnostics) |  |
| ✓ cataloged birth provenance for downstream hierarchy initialization |  |

### Parameters

| Name | Meaning | Units | Typical range | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `primary_imf` | any IMF card's model (house default: the SMOOTH Maschberger) | sampled masses in Msun | — | `build_binary_cluster(primary_imf=...) or build_cataloged_binary_cluster(primary_imf=...)` |
| `companion_model` | IndependentCompanions (separable) or MoeCompanions (faithful P-q-e) | — | — | `build_binary_cluster(companion_model=...) or build_cataloged_binary_cluster(companion_model=...)` |
| `target` | population size specification: Systems(n) / Stars(n) / TotalMass(M) | count or Msun | — | `build_binary_cluster(target=...) or build_cataloged_binary_cluster(target=...)` |

### Equations

```{math}
:label: card-assembly-com
\sum_{\mathrm{pair}} m_j \mathbf{v}_j \;=\; \Bigl(\sum_{\mathrm{pair}} m_j\Bigr)\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{sys}} \quad \text{and} \quad \frac{\sum_{\mathrm{pair}} m_j \mathbf{r}_j}{\sum_{\mathrm{pair}} m_j} \;=\; \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{sys}}
```

*Symbols:* $m_j$: component mass, summed over the pair [native dynamical mass units]; $\mathbf{v}_j$: component velocity in the cluster frame [native velocity units]; $\mathbf{r}_j$: component position in the cluster frame [native length units]; $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{sys}}$: system COM velocity before orbital resolution [native velocity units]; $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{sys}}$: system COM position before orbital resolution [native length units].
*Assumes:* internal barycentric position and momentum offsets sum to zero; translating to the cluster frame preserves the system COM and total momentum.

### Sources

- {cite:t}`MoeDiStefano2017` — the faithful companion statistics option (see moe_pqe) *(Table 13)*
- {cite:t}`MurrayDermott2000` — the orbital resolution (see kepler_elements) *(Ch. 2)*
